title: Live Tour
paragraphs: I… Is my proposal really that difficult? Creating a fake Filo-chan based on Sakura-chan is the best I can do right now… There’s no way I can give up on this. I’m going to start researching how to make Filo-chan and Sakura-chan coexist somehow. Let’s get Ren going!
“Well… aside from this National Library of Faubrey, there are all sorts of research materials lying dormant around the world, so wouldn’t it be a good idea to look into them?”
“Let’s put it on hold for now… Let’s have Rat-san help us with the Filolials’ health checks and research. We might even be able to identify the factors that determine the Filolials’ appearance.”
“That’s true. As a researcher, I’m interested in investigating that area, so I’ll cooperate. I look forward to working with you from now on.”

And just like that, Father negotiated and signed a contract with the Doctor. After wrapping up the discussion, we headed straight to meet up with Yuki-chan and the others, and decided to return to Siltvelt. Ah, Filo-tan. In this world, you’re so far away from me.
And so, we ended up heading from Siltvelt to Shieldfreeden.
“Motoyasu-kun, do you happen to have a portal to Shieldfreeden?”
“Unfortunately, it’s a country I’ve rarely had occasion to visit…”
I’ll activate the Portal Spear and check the history. Even though the number of registrable locations has increased now that we can allocate skills points, there’s still a limit.

As for my memories of Shieldfreeden, the only thing I really remember is stopping by during Filo-tan’s “IN Worldwide Live Tour.” Other than that, there was just a town like Zeltoble—a bit of a half-baked imitation. It had a Merlion statue and a half-baked “Vegas vibe,” I suppose. By the way, “Vegas” is just a nickname—it’s a town on Earth. I went there to hang out with Pig a long time ago.

I remember a huge commotion when a gang boss visiting the casino was killed by an assassin. In the midst of all that chaos, I grabbed a guy who was trying to kidnap Pig by the hair on his bald head and pinned him down. That’s not a contradiction, you know. Yeah… he had a nostalgic little braid on the back of his head that looked like a barcode, so I grabbed it.

I don’t know if he was one of that guy’s cronies, but there was another guy who actually had a barcode tattoo on the back of his head. Barcodes… they’re handy things you can just “beep” through a cash register. It brought back a memory of an older guy who lived in the neighborhood—he looked like an older brother to me—showing me some old toys. Apparently, you could even play games against each other using barcodes.

I wonder what kind of powerful piece I would’ve gotten if I’d scanned that code on the back of his head… Ever since I stopped thinking about pigs, that’s all I can seem to remember. Oh? It looks like Father in my memory is rolling his eyes, saying, “Why are you thinking about such trivial things?”
“There’s no portal to Shieldfreeden, is there?”
I thought we’d covered just about everything, but that’s quite the blind spot.
“Well, I guess we’ll just have to head there directly.”
“There’s a portal to a place closer than Siltvelt, so maybe we should set off from there?”
“That might be a good idea. If either Motoyasu or I take turns heading to the destination, we’ll save time too.”
“Heroes, please wait a moment.”
The people from Siltvelt are calling out to us.
“What’s the matter?”
“Regarding travel to Shieldfreeden, the Takt faction has proposed using an airplane they confiscated.”
“Huh? An airplane? Well… if we can use it, I guess it’s fine, but is it really safe? Doesn’t that require some pretty specialized technical know-how?”
“Our investigation has confirmed that it’s operational. We’ve also been told there are no issues with fuel.”
“Well, we’ll take you up on that… but I’d hate to get into an accident while we’re traveling.”
It is an airplane in a different world, after all. That said, I don’t think we’ll have any trouble, do we?
“I don’t think there’ll be any problems. As far as I know, within this loop, planes and airships confiscated from the Takt faction have been used before.”
“Well, if that’s the case, then we’ll be fine.”
“Yes. We’ve determined that the plane we’ll be using this time is the one that previously traveled from Melromarc to Siltvelt.”
“That’s the one that brought the guys over, right? That seems like a bad omen.”
We’re invading an enemy country and got beaten back, after all. And so, with that plane—confiscated from Takt and used to transport the guys from Melromarc to Siltvelt—we set off for Shieldfreeden.
As for the plane… I thought it would be a jet airliner, but it’s a bit more compact. It looks a lot like the kind used for parachuting. Flying in a plane like that… well, it lacks a certain elegance.
“Whoa, this is so cool!”
“The view isn’t bad at all.”
“It’s sooo high!”
Yuki-chan and the others are voicing their impressions as they gaze out at the scenery from the plane. Since Filolial-sama fundamentally cannot fly, she really loves heights.
“It’s a great experience to get to ride in something like an airplane, but it’s a scary place if something were to happen.”
Panda murmurs, looking slightly wary.
“Well, yeah…”
“If anything happens, I’ll jump out of the plane, hoist Father onto my back, and land on the ground with a big somersault.”
“That’s a pretty surreal image to picture, though…”
“You’ve got to do what you’ve got to do.”
Flutter, flutter, flutter! Let’s practice that later. Ha! It’d be great to incorporate that into Third Mode, too!
“I’d rather not, if possible… Are Sakura-chan and the others okay?”
“If I spread my wings, I can catch the air. I don’t think the damage will be as bad as you’d think.”
“Is that how it works?”
“After that, if I use Wind Magic to slow our descent and dissipate the impact, we’ll be fine.”
It’s theoretically possible. I think Lord Filolial could pull it off with ease.
“Magic sure is convenient, isn’t it?”
“Actually, I heard this earlier myself. Apparently, the main thing to watch out for when piloting an airplane is not crashing into monsters flying in the sky. Next up are floating reefs.”
“The skies in this other world are pretty inconvenient, aren’t they? Is that why airplane technology hasn’t really taken off?”
Father looks exhausted and has a distant look in his eyes.
“Well, from my perspective, traveling on a giant flying dragon is still more relaxing, I suppose…”
“But Motoyasu wouldn’t like that. Sure, they’re fast and convenient, but I can’t believe Takt actually pushed for something like this.”
“Well, he is a reincarnated person, after all.”
“Come to think of it, what kind of person was Takt in his past life? If we strip away the unnecessary parts of Takt’s life, might we get a glimpse of who he really was?”

Father began analyzing the situation with great interest. I’m not really good at this kind of speculation, you see. It’s not that I can’t do it—I just usually end up getting it wrong. I do get it right once in a while, but since Father is more likely to be correct than I am, I’d better just stop trying.
“Let’s rule out ‘womanizer’… He was mass-producing and developing firearms… and he was also having airplanes built.”
Father narrowed his eyes as he gazed out the airplane window.

“Maybe he was a military hobbyist or something like that? He seemed to be pushing technologies that are inefficient according to the laws of this world, like guns… On a global scale, the only thing that wouldn’t be a problem is probably papermaking technology at best.”
“Isn’t paper something that can be made easily?”
“That might depend on the situation. There are various plants that are well-suited for making paper, after all. Apparently, parchment was also quite common in this world…”
“Well, when it comes to paper, it’s certainly true that the modern Faubrey popularized it. Thanks to that, the price of that kind of paperwork definitely went down.”
“I suppose you could say productivity improved…?　And then there was the shift from acidic paper to neutral paper… or something like that?”
“I’ve heard that too. Neutral paper is the kind that lasts for many years, isn’t it?”
“Yeah. In our world, old paper used to deteriorate quickly, but lately they’ve switched to neutral paper, which lasts longer.”
“……Huh? Come to think of it, I seem to recall a conversation like that before the loop.”
It’s nothing to talk about—just a memory from after the first world became peaceful. My grumpy Father was grumbling while looking at some paper, I think.
“If I remember correctly… something about the paper Takt promoted not lasting very long or something like that……”

“……So the plant-based paper commonly used in this world has properties similar to neutral paper, and what Takt promoted was acidic paper? Even if it’s cheaper, isn’t that unsuitable for long-term preservation?”
That’s putting the cart before the horse. Takt really is a menace. I suppose there were all sorts of hidden motives behind even a single one of his inventions.

Father used neutral paper as an example, but my future father, if I recall correctly… referred to it as a “cheap, mass-produced product.” It’s high-quality and low-cost right after it’s made, but the quality deteriorates faster than usual… they say it’s “ahead-of-its-time” quality. On the other hand, Fathers said it’s actually harder to make something like this.
“It seems the inventions of reincarnated individuals tend to avoid leaving information behind for the future.”
In that sense, the Takt must have already been wreaking havoc across the world. I hear that if you give it a good shake, countless bits of dust come pouring out.
“In terms of demand, it’s not necessarily a bad thing… but if that’s the case, this airplane seems likely to have its own set of problems, too.”
“I believe craftsmen from various countries have gone on to resolve those issues to some extent…”

This is also quite vague. However, I do recall that Father discussed various matters with his Finacées and worked them out. At the very least, there continued to be a fair amount of demand for flying machines afterward.

I imagine the engineers from Zeltoble and others also cooperated to identify the issues. While Faubrey was already a famous attraction back when Takt had a monopoly on it, it seems they kept their internal operations tightly guarded.

Well, since it was a vehicle he used for his own travel, Takt probably didn’t cut any corners. I’ve also heard that it was his underlings who actually brought his ideas to life. Apparently, it was only thanks to Takt’s financial backing that aircraft—which had fallen into decline due to flying monsters—were recreated, or so the story goes.
“I seem to recall that, in the end, it mostly amounted to nothing more than a form of entertainment.”
“Well… in this world, there are monsters that, if you take care of them, become handy vehicles… and depending on the species, some people can fly, too.”
“Apparently, the reason Takt was able to operate airplanes and airships so effectively was that he raised dragons and other creatures to keep monsters at bay.”
“Ah… so it was a strategy to keep monsters at bay using the Ki emitted by high-ranking monsters… If that’s the logic, are we safe?”
“No problem at all. Even if they attack, I’ll open the door and unleash an Aiming Lancer.”
Destroy, that is. Let’s use them to boost our EXP.
“I kind of get what you mean, but… can’t Sakura-chan and the others be used to ward off monsters?”
“The Filolials are angels who preside over compassion. Warding off monsters would be quite difficult for them.”
“There are a few things that bother me, but since we can’t fly, maybe they’re underestimating us…”

But Filo-tan can fly, you know. I believe she gained the ability to fly thanks to Father’s power. Ah… come to think of it, if Father who made Filo-tan able to fly back then were here, he might have shown us a way to balance things between Sakura-chan and Filo-tan. …I wonder if tFather will become like that Father from back then? I can’t help but have a little hope.
“Motoyasu-kun? Is there something on my face? You’re looking at me funny.”
“I’m hoping a situation doesn’t arise where Father starts referring to himself and me as ‘I’ and ‘me’.”
“I doubt that’ll happen, though. What kind of character is that?”
“Wasn’t it the ‘evil alchemist’ character?”
“I’ve been through a lot and seem to have become a bit twisted. The ‘me’ that Motoyasu-kun knows… Still, I’m not sure I’d go that far.”
Father remarked that the conversation had somehow gone off track. It certainly had. …We were supposed to be talking about Takt.

“If you look into Takt’s achievements, you’ll probably find plenty of flaws—or rather, Darkness… Like the tragedies unfolding behind the scenes of cases solved by the story’s protagonist—I’m sure there are plenty of those.”
“That’s a problem we’ve faced too. Problems caused by me—who solved cases using my gaming knowledge—or by Ren and Itsuki—there were countless of them, really.”

For me, it was the Bio Plant running amok; for Ren, the dragon zombies and the ecological chaos; and for Itsuki, the revolution that never really found a fundamental solution. As for Father… I later learned there was a surge in accessory prices.

Apparently, accessories featuring the Divine Bird’s Carriage—the one pulled by Filo-chan—became a craze for a while, leading to problems like theft. If you look at the bigger picture, there are probably countless issues like that lying around.

However… I heard that in Takt’s case, it was all matters where only the people he’d taken under his wing stood to gain. When Takt and his group were executed, there was an engineer who rejoiced with both hands raised… wasn’t there? As was revealed in the previous loop, he’s apparently a total cheapskate.

There were also stories that a staggering amount of money was found in Takt’s house. Apparently, he’d been hoarding it for no reason. To save money without ever spending it—that’s the height of foolishness. Presumably, in this loop as well, it will be confiscated and distributed among the victims.

“Yeah… I suppose that’s how it is. We aren’t omniscient, omnipotent gods, after all. We’ll do our best to resolve things, but when it comes to problems we simply can’t solve… we’ll have to draw the line somewhere, I guess.”

It’s a difficult problem, isn’t it? Ultimately, it means that no matter what we do, there will be those who gain and those who lose. This isn’t the same as the “resources” that Father was talking about last time, but as long as resources are finite, we have to make choices somewhere along the line.
